questions_and_answers.question_text: What is túpiàn usually used for?
What is the literal meaning of xīnkǔ?
Write the Chinese for "Growing grain is the business of the peasants."
Write the Chinese for "You're going to get sick from fatigue by working so hard."
Write the Chinese for "It's too tiring for her, working during the daytime and studying at night."

answers.answer_text: Tā báitian zuò shì, wǎnshang niàn shū, tài xīnkǔ le.
"Special line, field, or discipline" — in the PRC, one's college major or professional specialization.

articles.text:
12. A: Cóng túpiànshang kàn, nǐmen    From the picture it looks like you're
       gōngzuòde hǎo xīnkǔ.          working very hard.
    B: Méiyou shénme xīnkǔ, jiù shi Not so hard. We're just planting some
       zài xuéxiào hòubianr zhòng    vegetables behind the school.
       diǎnr cài.

13. zhuānyè      special line/field/discipline
14. jīqì (jīqi)  machine

Notes on No. 12

túpiàn: "picture, photograph." This is usually used for PHOTOGRAPHS, as in túpiàn zhǎnlǎn, "photo exhibition" (but some people use it for any kind of illustration).

xīnkǔ: "to be arduous, tiring, hard" (literally, "PUNGENT-BITTER")

Tā báitian zuò shì, wǎnshang     It's too tiring for her, working during
niàn shū, tài xīnkǔ le.          the daytime and studying at night.
Nǐ zhème xīnkǔ yào lèibìngde.    You're going to get sick from fatigue by
                                 working so hard.

zhòng: "to plant" or "to grow" things:

Zhèikuài dì zhòng shénme yě bù   You don't harvest anything you plant on
shōu.                            this land!
Zhòng liángshi shi nóngmínde     Growing grain is the business of the
shì.                             peasants.
Zhèige shǎoshù mínzú zài         This minority nationality grows a lot of
shānshang zhòngle bù shǎo        strange things on the mountain to eat.
qíguàide dōngxi lái chī.
